title: France – Repair and maintenance of plant – RENOVATION DES DEGRILLEURS/SKIP DES STATIONS DE RELEVAGE DE L'EPERVIERE ET DE CHAFFIT
description: L’aménagement hydroélectrique de Beauchastel dispose de trois stations de relevage : la station de Blaud, la station de Chaffit et la station de l’Épervière. Chacune de ces stations est équipée de pompes permettant d’assurer le relevage des eaux provenant des canaux de fuite des digues. Elles disposent également de dégrilleurs automatiques de type « râteaux », destinés à assurer le nettoyage des grilles amont et à évacuer les détritus retenus par celles-ci. Historiquement, les quatre dégrilleurs présents sur les trois stations étaient de conception similaire et de fabrication JONNERET. En 2024, deux de ces équipements ont été entièrement remplacés par des dégrilleurs neufs, leur état de dégradation ayant été jugé incompatible avec une rénovation. Dans le cadre de la remise à niveau de ses installations, CNR souhaite désormais rénover les deux dégrilleurs restants. Le périmètre des travaux comprend également la rénovation d'un équipement de levage destinés à la manutention et à l’évacuation des détritus, situé sur le site de l’Épervière. Les trois stations de relevage ont été mises en service en 1966. Compte tenu de l’ancienneté des installations, le marché comprendra des travaux de nature mécanique et électrique visant à remettre à niveau les équipements concernés, à améliorer leur fiabilité et à garantir leur pérennité. Une part de rétroconception mécanique sera également à prévoir. En effet, CNR ne dispose pas de l’ensemble des plans de détail d’origine relatifs à certains équipements. Le titulaire devra donc, lorsque nécessaire, réaliser les relevés dimensionnels et investigations permettant de reconstituer les données techniques indispensables à la conception et à la réalisation des travaux. Les travaux sont programmés en 2027 sur le site de l'Epervière, et en 2028 sur le site de Chaffit (option).

title: PCB Transformer Replacements at Beaver Creek Institution -Minimum
description: The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requires the removal and replacement of two transformers at Beaver Creek Institution (Minimum) prior to December 31, 2026 to comply with federal regulations established under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act and the polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) Regulations. One existing pad-mounted transformer, installed in 1975, contains polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) at a concentration of 172 ppm, which exceeds the regulatory threshold. A second pole-mounted transformer has reached the end of its service life and, due to its age, may contain PCBs. Both transformers must be removed and replaced prior to the regulatory deadline of December 31, 2026. The work includes the supply and installation of replacement transformers, disposal of PCB-contaminated equipment and associated oil in accordance with applicable regulations, coordination of electrical outages and commissioning activities, and restoration of affected areas.

title: Request for Offers for the provision of Cleaning Services for the Embassy of Canada to Lebanon, in Beirut
description: The cleaning services must be delivered at The Canadian Embassy to Lebanon, in Beirut. The work includes the provision of routine and periodic cleaning services, as well as any additional cleaning required to meet operational needs. Services must be provided in accordance with the specifications outlined in this Statement of Work and must support a clean, safe, and professional environment at all times while not interfering with the daily operations or activities of the building’s occupants, clients, or visitors. The Canadian Embassy in Beirut, Lebanon is in Spark Tower Bldg, 2415 Sin El Fil, Beirut, Lebanon, a business centre comprising 18 Floors. The total surface area occupied by the embassy is of 3550 m2 and comprises: part of the Ground Floor, the Fourteenth floor, the Fifteenth floor, the Sixteenth floor, the Mezzanine in the Sixteenth floor, the Seventeenth floor, parking spaces, storage rooms, guards and drivers’ rooms. While the majority of the work will be located at the Chancery Building of the Embassy located in Sin El Fil, cleaning staff may be called upon to provide similar work at the Official Residence of the Ambassador or at the apartments of the Embassy’s diplomatic staff in Ashrafieh, or at any other venue as required by the Embassy of Canada. title: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the item detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is required as the first step of an explosive shockwave in an explosive train when using a non-electric method of initiation. It is functioned by inserting an igniferous burning fuse into the open end and being crimped onto the burning fuse. When the flame from the burning fuse exits the end of the fuse, it ignites a primary explosive composition which in turn transfers a shockwave into the secondary explosive component in the Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7. The Cap Blasting Non-Electric M7 is primarily used in military applications for demolition purposes. Quantity: 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan on or before 01 November 2027. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario on or before 01 November 2027. 3,000 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Dundurn, Dundurn, Saskatchewan between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. 3,500 units - Delivery to Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot (CFAD) Angus, Angus, Ontario between 01 September 2028 and 30 November 2028. title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in D-98646 Hildburghausen - Generalplanung nach §§ 34, 51, 55 HOAI 2021 sowie Besondere Leistungen
description: Das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad in Hildburghausen ist seit der Errichtung und Einweihung im Jahr 2000 ein zentraler und wichtiger Bestandteil der regionalen Infrastruktur, da es eine unverzichtbare Funktion in den Bereichen Sport, Bildung, Freizeit und Gesundheit erfüllt. Im Besonderen ist hier die Funktion für die Schwimmausbildung im Rahmen des Schulschwimmens für den kompletten Landkreises Hildburghausen zu nennen. Als Ganzjahresbad mit einer Kombination aus Hallen- und Freibadbereich sichert es die Schwimmausbildung für Schulen und Vereine in der Region und dient als wichtige Trainingsstätte für den lokalen Sport. Die große Badelandschaft mit 25 m-Bahnen und Sprungturm ist essenziell für die allgemeine Fitness und das sportliche Training. Darüber hinaus ist das Bad ein beliebtes regionales Ausflugsziel und ein wichtiger sozialer Treffpunkt. Mit Attraktionen wie der 50 m-Riesenrutsche, einem Spaßbecken mit Massagedüsen und einem separaten Kinderplanschbecken bietet es einen wetterunabhängigen Anziehungspunkt für Familien und Erholungssuchende aus dem gesamten Landkreis. Ergänzt wird dieses Angebot durch eine Saunalandschaft, die den Aspekt Wellness und Gesundheitsförderung abdeckt. Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen, dass das Werra Sport- und Freizeitbad weit über die Funktion eines einfachen Schwimmbades hinausgeht: Es steigert die Lebensqualität der Bürger und bildet eine tragende Säule der Freizeit- und Sportinfrastruktur in Hildburghausen und Süddthüringen. Während die lange diskutierte und komplexe Sanierung des Freibadbereiches im Jahr 2024 abgeschlossen werden konnte, steht nun die umfassende Ertüchtigung der Schwimmhalle selbst an. Trotz einer kleineren Sanierung der Halle im Jahr 2018 sind die technischen Anlagen, die Gebäudehülle und die Innenbereiche nach über zwei Jahrzehnten intensiver Nutzung in einem Zustand, der eine Generalüberholung notwendig macht. Diese Sanierung muss deutlich über kosmetische Reparaturen hinausgehen und die technische, energetische und gestalterische Modernisierung der gesamten Halle sowie der angeschlossenen Saunalandschaft umfassen. Ziel ist es, den Energieverbrauch langfristig zu senken und das Bad zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Sanierung des Werra Sport- und Freizeitbades ist eine komplexe und anspruchsvolle Planungsaufgabe, für die ein kompetentes Planerteam gesucht wird. Die Brutto-Grundfläche des Gebäudes (BGF) beträgt ca. 3.600 m2. Die Wasserfläche umfasst ca. 480 m2. Für die geplante Maßnahme werden Baukosten von ca. 4,0 Mio Euro (Brutto, KG 300 und 400) veranschlagt.

title: NATO Business Opportunity: Project, Program, and Portfolio Management (P3M) Training
description: Headquarters, Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (HQ SACT) has issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) to provide Project, Program, and Portfolio Management (P3M) Training. The contractor shall provide comprehensive, on-site training courses for HQ personnel. The baseline scope requires the delivery of six P3M courses per calendar year. The selected training qualifications must be capable of accelerating a student from zero baseline knowledge to the Practitioner level within a maximum of five consecutive days. Prospective Bidders should seek clarification at their earliest convenience. Any explanation regarding the meaning or interpretation of this RFP, terms, clause, provision or specifications, shall be requested in writing, from the Contracting Officer. All Contracting Officers listed on this RFP must receive such requests via email for clarification no later than 27 October 2026. Bids shall be received at HQ SACT, Purchasing and Contracting Office, no later than 05 November 2026, 0900 hours. No bids shall be accepted after this date and time. No hard copy proposals will be accepted. Please see the RFP for more details. REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL Please see attached. BIDDING PROCEDURE A Declaration of Eligibility is NOT required for this opportunity. Do NOT submit your proposal to the Department of Commerce. Please submit your proposal directly to HQ SACT using the contact information provided in the RFP.

title: ASIT.TO 1 year software support from ArgonSoft (Notice of Intent to sole source)
description: Acquisition Description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with ArgonSoft. The National Institute of Health (NIH) requires software maintenance and support for the NIH Laboratory Information Management system (LIMS) called ASIS.TO which is designed by Argonsoft. The LIMS was previously installed by ArgonSoft in the NIH CC/ET department under agreement # 75N90023P00826. The required software and support includes: 1 year gold system support, installation of mandatory updates and minor upgrade package, and IQ/OQ of running installation and operation qualification tests. Justification: Argonsoft is the creator and license holder for their software, and they directly provide support and renewal to their software. Thus, they are the sole source vendor that can provide the software maintenance of this customized proprietary software. Place of Performance or Delivery: The estimated Period of Performance is: January 1, 2026 � December 31, 2026 Place of Performance: NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, MD The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 1901 (a) (1) as implemented by FAR 13.106-1 only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. title: Pre-Solicitation Site Visit: Leavenworth Redundant Core Project
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FCI Leavenworth � Redundant Core, Radio Tower, and Shelter Installation Request for Industry Feedback & Announcement of Pre-Solicitation Site Visit THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE only. This notice is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is seeking industry feedback on the attached Statement of Work (SOW) for the planned installation of a Redundant Core Radio System, including a 100-foot communications tower, hardened equipment shelter, and associated integration services at FCI Leavenworth, Leavenworth, Kansas. The Government intends to use the information received from industry to refine requirements, evaluate capability within the market, identify potential sources, and inform the acquisition strategy. PROJECT OVERVIEW The purpose of this project is to establish a fully interoperable Redundant Core for the BOP�s enterprise radio network. The installation at FCI Leavenworth will provide operational continuity and Core?level backup for FCC Victorville and FCC Allenwood, ensuring uninterrupted communications in the event of system failure or required maintenance at either location. Detailed technical requirements are provided in the attached SOW. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION / INDUSTRY FEEDBACK The Government requests that interested vendors review the attached SOW and provide: Comments, recommendations, or questions regarding clarity, feasibility, assumptions, and risk areas. Capability statements demonstrating experience with: Installation of P25 Phase II trunked radio systems Tower construction compliant with ANSI/TIA?222 standards Secure communications shelters and hardened infrastructure Core-level radio system integrations Feedback on schedule, phasing, and deliverables included in the SOW. Potential subcontracting opportunities (if applicable). Responses are voluntary and will not affect participation in any future solicitation. SITE VISIT ANNOUNCEMENT A site visit will be offered to all interested vendors. Interested vendors are strongly encouraged to attend this site visit. The Government may not offer an additional site visit during the formal solicitation period. Date: November 5, 2026 Time: 8:30 a.m. (local time) Location: FCI Leavenworth, Leavenworth, KS Due to security requirements, NCIC background check forms must be submitted and approved in advance for all individuals attending the site visit. Vendors are strongly encouraged to submit forms early to ensure access is granted. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested vendors should submit NCIC forms to Tanner Marshall for processing. Interested vendors should submit the following information to Kasie Redman, Contracting Officer, for market research: Company name, DUNS/UEI, CAGE code Point of contact information Business size/category under the applicable NAICS code Responses to feedback questions listed above Any additional information the vendor considers relevant Responses are requested by: Friday, October 18, 2026 (NCIC Forms submitted ONLY to Tanner Marshall at tmarshall@bop.gov) Thursday, November 5, 2026 (Interested Party information for market research) Responses should be submitted via email to: Kasie Redman, Contracting Officer Email: k2redman@bop.gov DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought Notice is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with participation in this notice or the pre-solicitation site visit.

title: Body, Retainer, and Gasket
description: General Information This is a solicitation for non-commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Body, Retainer, and Gasket parts. This solicitation will be competed as a total small business set-aside. Solicitation Details Quotes are being requested under Request for Quotations (RFQ) N0017426Q1120. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 332710 and the associated small business size standard is 500 employees. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the FAR/RFO. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20260507. Technical Drawings If interested, technical drawings need to be requested by contractor prior to submission date. ITAR certification is required to be provided prior to technical drawing release. Drawing requests must be made via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil by Friday, 23 October 2026, 10:00 AM EST. Drawings will be send via DoD Safe. Cybersecurity Compliance Requirement (CMMC Level 1): For purposes of technically acceptability, the Offeror shall submit documentation verifying an active CMMC Level 1 Self-Assessment recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). If the Offeror does not possess an active SPRS entry at the time of proposal submission, the Offeror will not be deemed technically acceptable. Basis for Award The Government will award a purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible vendor whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government intends to evaluate all timely quotes received from eligible vendors on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and award a purchase order without discussion. Evaluation Factors: Technical: Quotes must reflect the required specifications and the exact brand specified in the Statement of Work. Price: Quotes must include all applicable costs, including shipping and handling. Questions and Clarifications Questions regarding this requirement must be submitted via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil no later than Friday, 16 October 2026. All answers will be provided by Friday, 23 October 2026. Submission Instructions Quote packages are due by November 6th, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST. Late quotes will not be considered. Quote packages shall be sent via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil and must contain a cover sheet that provides the following information: Official Company Name; Point of Contact (including name, email address, and phone number); and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code.

title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Spent Fuel Cell Shipment(s)
description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Center for Neutron Research (NCNR) owns and operates a 20 MW test reactor called the National Bureau of Standards Reactor (NBSR) located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. The NBSR is fueled by 30 highly enriched uranium fuel elements. During the course of a year, the NBSR produces approximately 28 spent fuel elements. To be in accordance with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), NIST is required to transfer its spent fuel to the Department of Energy (DOE) Savannah River Site (SRS) near Aiken, South Carolina. This requirement is for one base shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2028, with an option for a second shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2030. See attached solicitation# 1333ND27QNB610AMD and related attachments for full details.

description: General Information This is a solicitation for non-commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for Body, Retainer, and Gasket parts. This solicitation will be competed as a total small business set-aside. Solicitation Details Quotes are being requested under Request for Quotations (RFQ) N0017426Q1120. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 332710 and the associated small business size standard is 500 employees. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the FAR/RFO. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20260507. Technical Drawings If interested, technical drawings need to be requested by contractor prior to submission date. ITAR certification is required to be provided prior to technical drawing release. Drawing requests must be made via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil by Friday, 23 October 2026, 10:00 AM EST. Drawings will be send via DoD Safe. Cybersecurity Compliance Requirement (CMMC Level 2): For purposes of technical acceptability, the Offeror shall submit documentation verifying a current CMMC Level 2 status�either Conditional or Final, as applicable�recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). If the Offeror does not possess a current CMMC Level 2 status in SPRS at the time of proposal submission, the Offeror will not be deemed technically acceptable. Basis for Award The Government will award a purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible vendor whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government intends to evaluate all timely quotes received from eligible vendors on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and award a purchase order without discussion. Evaluation Factors: Technical: Quotes must reflect the required specifications and the exact brand specified in the Statement of Work. Price: Quotes must include all applicable costs, including shipping and handling. Questions and Clarifications Questions regarding this requirement must be submitted via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil no later than Friday, 16 October 2026. All answers will be provided by Friday, 23 October 2026. Submission Instructions Quote packages are due by November 6th, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST. Late quotes will not be considered. Quote packages shall be sent via email to deanna.l.wilson27.civ@us.navy.mil and must contain a cover sheet that provides the following information: Official Company Name; Point of Contact (including name, email address, and phone number); and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code.

description: SUMMARY The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 5, is issuing this Sources Sought Notice to identify vendors that are interested in and capable of providing the required services. The Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center, located in Clarksburg, WV, requires a contractor to provide Triennial Electrical System Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance for the facility. Interested vendors should review the Statement of Work (SOW) to determine the specific services required. Johnson VA Medical Center (LAJ VAMC), Clarksburg, West Virginia. The intent of this work is to verify the integrity, reliability, and code compliance of the in-scope electrical equipment, identify and correct deficiencies, and provide the documentation required to satisfy The Joint Commission (TJC), CMS Conditions of Participation, NFPA, and VA accreditation/inspection requirements for the elements within scope. 1.2 Background LAJ VAMC is a VHA Complexity Level 2 medical center within VISN 5. The campus electrical distribution serves Type 1 Essential Electrical Systems under NFPA 99 (Life Safety, Critical, and Equipment Branches). Buildings within scope include the main hospital, Boiler Plant, building 7, Building 20, the Clinical Addition, and supporting structures. The previous comprehensive triennial electrical inspection was performed in CY 2023; this procurement covers the CY 2026 cycle for the in-scope equipment. Generator triennial preventive maintenance and 3-year load bank testing (NFPA 110-2025 §8.4.2), the arc flash risk assessment / coordination study refresh, and any campus power quality / harmonics survey are being procured under separate contract vehicles and are NOT within the scope of this SOW. 1.3 Objective Achieve and document one hundred percent (100%) compliance with all applicable codes and standards listed in Section 3.0 for the equipment categories within scope, including but not limited to NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), NFPA 70B-2023, NFPA 70E-2024, NFPA 99-2024, NFPA 101-2024, NFPA 111-2022, ANSI/NETA MTS-2023, VHA Directive 1028, and VA PG-18-10. 1.4 Definitions and Acronyms Acronym Definition AHJ Authority Having Jurisdiction ATS Automatic Transfer Switch CHENG / DCE Chief Engineer / Deputy Chief Engineer COR Contracting Officer's Representative EES Essential Electrical System (NFPA 99 Type 1) GFCI Ground-Fault Circuit Interrupter IRT Infrared Thermography LAJ VAMC Louis A. Functional testing and exercising of all Automatic Transfer Switches (ATSs) on the Life Safety, Critical, and Equipment Branches. Protective relay testing, calibration, and trip-curve verification on all MV and selected LV electronic-trip breakers (settings verified against the existing Government-furnished coordination study; no study revision performed under this SOW). Insulation resistance, contact resistance, and primary injection testing of LV power circuit breakers; secondary injection where applicable. Ground electrode and grounding system resistance testing (3-point fall-of-potential). Energized infrared thermographic survey of all electrical equipment from service entrance through branch panelboards. Patient care space receptacle testing in accordance with NFPA 99-2024 §6.3.3.3 (line voltage, polarity, grounding integrity, retention force). UPS battery system inspection and testing in accordance with NFPA 111-2022 and IEEE 1188 (VRLA) / IEEE 450 (vented). Documentation reconciliation of in-scope equipment maintenance records, deficiency reporting, and final triennial test report package. 2.2 Out of Scope (Procured Under Separate Contracts) The following are EXCLUDED from this contract and are being procured under separate contract vehicles: Generator triennial preventive maintenance and the NFPA 110-2025 §8.4.2 three-year load bank testing of the four (4) facility emergency standby generators. title: Request for Information (RFI) - OCONUS Generator Maintenance
description: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Request for Information (RFI) Outside Continental United States locations (OCONUS) Generator Maintenance 10/15/2026 The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Logistics Management Directorate, is conducting market research to identify contractors capable of providing on-site generator maintenance and testing services at four Outside Continental United States locations (OCONUS). The anticipated requirement may include key personnel, technician labor, specialized tooling, diagnostic instruments, vehicles, materials, consumables, transportation, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, testing, and related generator support services. The OCONUS requirement encompasses generator assets across three distinct island regions, comprising a total of five distinct operation locations: � Caribbean DC Caribbean: Rd.1, Km 25.1, Quebrada Arenas Ward, Caguas, PR 00725 Ponce Warehouse: 1000 Carr 507, Coto Laurel, PR 00780 � Hawaii DC Hawaii: 99-1269 Iwaena Street, Aiea, HI 96701 East Range: 1980 Higgins Road, Bldg. 6043, Wahiawa, HI 96786 � Guam DC Guam Bldg. 100, Barriagada GU 96913 This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the LMD Outside Continental United States Generator Maintenance (OCONUS Generator Maintenance). In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Respondents shall identify any proprietary information in their RFI response. Information submitted in response to this RFI will be used at the discretion of the Government. Further, the information submitted will remain confidential insofar as permitted by law, including the Freedom of Information and Privacy Acts. FEMA reserves the right to utilize any non-proprietary technical information in the anticipated PWS or solicitation. Although it is not necessary to address in their response, respondents shall be aware of any potential, actual, or perceived organizational conflicts of interest. Any real or potential conflicts must be sufficiently mitigated prior to a contract award. For further guidance, refer to the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 3.12 NAICS CODE: 811310 PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): J061, Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Electric Wire, and Power and Distribution Equipment ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE START DATE: 06/30/2027 ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: To be determined based on market research results ATTACHMENT: OCONUS Generator Inventory Summary October 2026 (.xlsx) Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Oneko Dunbar, Contracting Officer, at Oneko.Dunbar@fema.dhs.gov and Marcia Irizarry-Snyder, Contract Specialist at Marcia.Irizarrysnyder@fema.dhs.gov no later than 11:00 am Eastern Time (ET) November 5, 2026. Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than 11:00 am ET October 21, 2026.

title: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on or about 15 September 2026, online through Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov; therefore, requests for hardcopies of the solicitation will not be honored. .The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the small business size standard is $45Million.In order to submit a Bid on this project, your company must-1) Be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) and maintain an active registration status. 2) Be registered in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) for the Solicitation Module with the PROPOSAL MANAGER role. title: Notice of Proposed Contract Action- Keysight PNT-X Maintenance Renewal
description: In accordance with RFO FAR 5.101 and FAR Class Deviation (Number 25-17), this is a notification of a proposed contract action to Keysight Technologies Inc. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) intends to solicit and award on a sole source basis under authority RFO FAR 12.102 (a), FAR Class Deviation Number 25-21, to Keysight Technologies Inc., 1900 Garden of the Gods Road, Colorado Springs, CO 80907-3423, United States. This procurement is being conducted under Simplified Acquisition Procedures (SAP)- only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) has a requirement for annual license maintenance, referred to as Gold Maintenance and Support Bundle, to provide technical support for the Keysight Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT)-X global navigation satellite system radio frequency simulator. The USCG, as an agency of the DHS, is a multi-mission maritime service. To support position, navigation, and timing of Coast Guard assets in support of the mission, the Coast Guard has obtained and used the Keysight PNT-X global navigation satellite system radio frequency simulator. The simulator is used to test global positioning system receivers used by Coast Guard assets including their performance in jamming and spoofing environments. This requirement for annual license support is in direct support of the simulator system. Keysight has been identified as the sole provider of the required maintenance and no other product or services can meet the Government�s requirement. All responsible sources may submit a bid, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. Interested vendors may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort in writing to the identified parties on or before 11:00 AM ET on 05 November 2026. All submissions must be submitted electronically via email. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed effort on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. This notice of intent is NOT a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for competitive quotes. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. Interested parties may submit any information for consideration by the Government to the Contract Specialist, Ann M. Leuters, Email: Ann.M.Leuters@uscg.mil and the Contracting Officer, Brian J. Eichelberger, Email: Brian.J.Eichelberger@uscg.mil with Notice ID number referenced in the subject line. All requests for consideration must be submitted electronically via email. Phone calls will not be accepted.

title: Mode5/TCAS/Surveillance Cloaking Capability
description: 1. Purpose This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research purposes only. The Government is seeking information from capable and interested businesses, including small businesses, that can provide systems engineering support for integration and test of Mode 5, Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS), and surveillance cloaking capability into two United States Marine Corps (USMC) Boeing C-40A Clipper aircraft. This notice is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Information received will be used to assess the availability of qualified sources, determine the extent of small-business capability, and inform the Government�s acquisition strategy. 2. Requirement Description The Government anticipates a requirement for systems engineering, avionics integration, and test support associated with incorporation of surveillance capability into two USMC Boeing C-40A Clipper aircraft. The anticipated place of performance is Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland. Additional travel or support at other Government or contractor locations may be required, as identified in any future solicitation or statement of work. The anticipated effort includes engineering analysis, integration planning, interface assessment, configuration management, installation support, ground- and flight-test planning and execution, anomaly resolution, technical-data development, and technical program support. The effort requires integration of the following avionics equipment: APX-119-540 Transponder � P/N 4079100-0540 Digital Control Panel (DCP) � P/N 4087561-0503 KIV-79 Crypto Applique � P/N 4079080-0503 Personality Module (PM) � P/N 4088953-0501 TPA-100B Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) Computer � P/N 940-0351-010 3. Anticipated Scope Potential sources should be capable of providing the following, as applicable: Review and analyze aircraft-level, system-level, and equipment-level requirements. Develop or update systems-engineering artifacts, interface-control documentation, integration plans, test plans, test procedures, and test reports. Assess aircraft electrical, mechanical, software, data-bus, antenna, display, and avionics interfaces associated with the identified equipment. Support aircraft modification planning, installation, and integration activities. Provide configuration-management, engineering-change, and technical-data support. Develop and execute, or support execution of, ground- and flight-test activities. Document test results, discrepancies, corrective actions, and recommended resolutions. Support Government-directed airworthiness, certification, operational test, or other approval activities, as applicable. Participate in technical interchange meetings, program reviews, risk-management activities, and status reporting. 4. Requested Capability Statement Interested parties are requested to submit a concise capability statement addressing the following: A. Company Information Company name, address, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier, if applicable. Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 488190. Primary technical and contracting points of contact, including telephone number and email address. B. Relevant Experience Experience within the past five years supporting systems engineering, modification, integration, testing, or sustainment of Boeing 737-derived aircraft, military transport aircraft, or comparable aircraft platforms. Experience integrating Mode 5/Identification Friend or Foe, transponder, TCAS, surveillance, cryptographic, or comparable mission-avionics systems. Experience with the specific avionics equipment identified in this notice, if applicable. Up to three relevant completed or ongoing efforts, including a short description of the work performed, period of performance, customer type, and the respondent�s role. C. Technical Capability Available systems-engineering, avionics-engineering, aircraft-electrical-engineering, software-engineering, test-engineering, flight-test-support, configuration-management, and technical-data capabilities. Capability to support integration planning, aircraft modification activities, ground testing, flight testing, troubleshooting, and discrepancy resolution. Relevant facilities, test equipment, engineering tools, specialized personnel, and other resources available to support this effort. Any anticipated Government-furnished equipment, Government-furnished information, technical-data, facility-access, or other support requirements. D. Teaming and Acquisition Input Whether the respondent intends to participate as a prime contractor, subcontractor, or teaming partner. Potential teaming arrangements and anticipated subcontracting requirements. Recommended acquisition approach, contract type, estimated period of performance, and major schedule considerations. Significant technical, supply-chain, schedule, airworthiness, test-resource, data-rights, or other risks the Government should consider. 5. Submission Instructions Responses shall be submitted electronically in PDF format no later than 12:00 p.m. on Thursday, November 5, 2026, to: Will Dagenhart william.j.dagenhart.civ@us.navy.mil The email subject line shall read: �Sources Sought Response � USMC C-40A Mode 5/TCAS/Surveillance Cloaking Integration Support � [Company Name]� Respondents shall clearly identify proprietary information contained in their responses. Do not submit classified, export-controlled, or otherwise sensitive information unless specifically authorized and transmitted through an approved Government process. 6. Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR PLANNING AND MARKET-RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION OR GUARANTEE THAT THE GOVERNMENT WILL ISSUE A SOLICITATION OR AWARD A CONTRACT. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE INFORMATION RECEIVED TO DETERMINE THE AVAILABILITY OF CAPABLE SOURCES AND EVALUATE POTENTIAL SMALL-BUSINESS PARTICIPATION OPPORTUNITIES.

title: 120mm Mortar Training Sytem
description: This Special Notice is to advise intrested memeber of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TREX II), as well as other intrested members within the U.S technology base, that a Request for Solutions (RFS) has been issued by Advanced Technology International (ATI) to develop a training device of the 120mm Mortar Training Sytem. The purpose the Training Readiness and Aceelerator (TREX II) is to spur innovative development, demonstration, and expedited delivery of prototypes to increase Warefighter readiness via modeling, simulation, education/ training, expermental validation, and miltary readiness focued projects. A constorium has been establised to develop prototypes presonnel and the support the platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DoD) or to improvement of platforms, systems, components of materials in use by the Armed Forces. Link for TREX II- https://www/trexii.org/ Objectives:STE LTS is seeking a training system for 120mm mortars in both the Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle (AMPV) and Stryker M1129 Mortar Carrier that: 1. Mortar crews can install and de-install. 2. Time to install and de-install is less than five minutes each. 3. Allows the use of a training round between 25 and 35 pounds. 4. Does not pose a safety hazard to the crew. 5. Allows adjust fire and multi fire for effect replication. A 120mm mortar has a maximum rate of fire of 16 rounds a minute.

title: Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX) Hosted by Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), and Including Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Tec
description: When: Thursday, 19 November 2026, 9:30 a.m. EST. The event will last approximately four hours. Where: Join us in person or virtually via Microsoft Teams. During registration, industry partners will be asked to indicate their preferred method of attendance (in person or virtual). Because venue capacity is limited, requesting in-person attendance does not guarantee an in-person invitation. In-person attendance will be limited to two representatives per entity. Invitations will generally be issued in registration order, subject to venue capacity and Government discretion, including consideration for first-time attendees. After registration closes, confirmed in-person attendees and virtual participants will receive the appropriate access information by email. Registration Closes: 5 Nov 2026 Ready to join us? Register using the link below. Please copy and paste the link into your browser rather than attempting to access it directly through SAM.gov: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Cx4WtRHSKa If you experience issues with the registration link, please contact us at: SMB_PAE_MC_CTIndustry@usmc.mil One quick favor before you hit submit: Please double-check your email address and telephone number. Your invitation and event information will be sent using the contact information you provide during registration. An incorrect email address means we will not be able to get your invitation to you. In the event of unforeseen technical issues, the virtual session may be cancelled. If that happens, presentation materials will be provided to registered attendees following the event. BACKGROUND Let�s Talk About What�s Next. Good acquisition starts with communication. Not just when a solicitation hits SAM.gov. Not just when proposals are due. And certainly not only after we already know exactly what we want to buy. Sometimes the most valuable conversation happens much earlier. On 19 November 2026, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) and Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L) invite industry to join us for our next quarterly Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX). Together with the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) and other Marine Corps acquisition and requirements stakeholders, we want to give industry a clearer look at where we're headed�and an opportunity to talk with the people helping us get there. The 19 November MCAX will provide industry with visibility into anticipated contracting opportunities across participating Marine Corps organizations, while creating dedicated time for questions and direct Government�Industry engagement. What are we looking for? Ideas. Capabilities. Competition. Innovation. And, most importantly, meaningful dialogue with industry partners who understand that supporting the Marine Corps begins with understanding the mission. Our senior leaders, Capability Portfolio Managers, acquisition professionals, PAE MC Rapid Capability Cell (RCC) representatives, and Small Business experts will share information about emerging requirements, acquisition priorities, and anticipated contracting opportunities across the Marine Corps enterprise. And we don't want the conversation to go only one way. MCAX is also our opportunity to hear from you. What are you seeing in the marketplace? Where is technology moving? What capabilities already exist that we should know about? And where can better communication between Government and Industry help us find smarter ways to meet the needs of the warfighter? That exchange matters. Because when Government better understands what industry can deliver�and industry better understands where the Marine Corps is going�we can have better conversations about how to get there. Whether you've supported the Marine Corps for decades, you're an innovative small business looking for your first opportunity, or you're somewhere in between, you're invited to be part of that conversation. Come hear what we're working on. Ask questions. Engage with the people behind the requirements. And gain a clearer understanding of where your capabilities may align with what comes next. EVENT FORMAT We know your time is valuable. That's why we're continuing to focus MCAX on the information and engagement that industry has told us matters most. The approximately four-hour live event is anticipated to include: Briefs from leaders in Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps, Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), PAE MC Cyber Technology Office, PAE MC RCC, and the Combat Development & Integration (CD&I) Capability Portfolio Managers (CPMs) Contract Opportunity Briefs from PAE MC, HQMC I&L and PAE MS Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) Industry Q&A We will continue streamlining formal presentations wherever possible so there is more time for meaningful engagement between Industry and Government. And because showing up prepared makes for a better conversation, we're giving you a head start. Before MCAX, take some time to explore the PAE MC Industry Portal at: https://www.pae.marines.mil/industry-portal/ The portal is designed to help industry learn more about PAE MC, our mission, and how to engage with us before the conversation begins. Have a capability we should know about? Industry partners are encouraged to submit capability briefs or white papers through the Industry Portal before the event. Sharing that information in advance gives our team an opportunity to better understand what you bring to the table and where your capabilities may connect with Marine Corps needs. A preview of selected contracting opportunities associated with the 19 November MCAX will also be added to this notice as soon as it becomes available. Industry partners are encouraged to check this notice periodically for updates prior to the event, review the opportunities in advance, and come ready to engage. HQMC I&L opportunities will be released to industry within five business days following the event through a separate SAM.gov announcement. One Mission. Many Opportunities. One Conversation Worth Having. We hope you'll join us on 19 November.

The solicitation will require a time charter of one US flagged or foreign flagged vessel (to be reflagged US prior to delivery of vessel) required to tow an acoustic array in support of U.S. Navy Operations. The vessel will tow a passive acoustic monitoring system, between 4-6 knots, 24hrs/day for up to a 60-day event. The ship will need to be able to tow on a directed heading within 5 degrees for extended periods at slow speed. Because of the type of acoustic system employed, the ability of the vessel to maintain heading stability is critical. The vessel must be capable of worldwide operations, including support in all ocean basins of the world from the Artic to the Antarctic during all periods of time. The vessel is expected to operate in open water in the vicinity of the Marginal Ice Zone (MIZ) and must be capable of surviving encounter with young open ice, as specified by ABS, Ice Class D0.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

Prosser Hatchery Sole Source Presolicitation Notice
description: Presolicitation Notice to Single Source Solicitation Number: W9127N27Q1CTI Agency: Department of the Army Office: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Location: USACE District, Portland Classification Code: F022 � Natural Resources/Conservation�Fish Hatchery NAICS Code: 112511 - Finfish Farming and Fish Hatcheries Notice Type: Presolicitation Notice Synopsis: This is a special notice prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO FAR) 5.101 �Presolicitation Notice� The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District (NWP) intends to negotiate/award a sole source contract with the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation (Yakama Nation). All requirements necessary will be provided for the annual acclimation and release of up to 1.1 million sub-yearling upriver bright (URB) fall Chinook juveniles (received from Little White Salmon Hatchery) and for an additional 210 thousand yearling URB fall Chinook juveniles (received from Bonneville Hatchery) at Prosser Hatchery; releases are expected to occur from May through June at 75 to 50 fish per pound and from March through April at 20 fish per pound, respectively. Additionally, Portland District will require Yakama Nation (YN) to supply 600,000 Upriver Bright (URB) Fall Chinook smolts (sourced entirely by Yakama Nation) to be released into the Yakima River from Prosser Hatchery at river mile 46.8; releases are expected to occur from May through June at fish sizes of 75 to 50 fish per pound. This fish production satisfies a portion of USACE�s mission in fulfilling mitigation obligations for The Dalles and John Day Dams. Pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2304(c)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation (DFARS) 206.302-1, only one responsible source and no other vendor will satisfy agency requirements. In 2008, the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) issued a revised Biological Opinion that concluded that the Federal Columbia River Power System jeopardizes the continued existence of various Endangered Species Act-listed anadromous fish in the Columbia River Basin. Jeopardy and adverse modification may be avoided by implementing reasonable and prudent alternatives (RPAs) composed of discrete actions covering, among other things, hatchery operations. RPA action number 40 calls for a review of the hatchery program associated with the mitigation for The Dalles and John Day Dams. After reviewing the program, USACE, among other agencies and organizations, ultimately arrived at a plan to move the hatchery operations into or above the exclusive Zone 6 Indian fishery to better meet mitigation objectives. Prosser Hatchery is situated just downstream of Prosser Dam at river kilometer 75 of the Yakima River. The Yakima River feeds into the Columbia River near Richland, Washington, above Zone 6. Prosser Hatchery possesses the appropriate water temperature, rearing pond space and availability during the required months to acclimate and release the subject fall Chinook juveniles into the Yakima River. No other acclimation and release facilities exist in, or near, the lower Yakima River that are 1) capable of acclimating these fish, and 2) not already in use by USACE for similar purposes. The underlying land, facilities and equipment at Prosser Hatchery are under the ownership of the Yakama Nation. Therefore, Yakama Nation has sole control and use of the facilities at Prosser Hatchery and does not permit other contractors to utilize these facilities. Regional fisheries experts from NMFS, USFWS and USACE agree that Prosser Hatchery is the only reasonable location to perform these specific rearing and release activities. The statutory authority for this non-competitive acquisition 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FRO FAR 6.103-1 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.103-170, there is only one responsible source, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE POSTED The Government intends to proceed with this sole source action. The NAICS code is 112511, Finfish Farming and Hatcheries. The size standard as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration is $3.75 million. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS Interested concerns must show clear and convincing evidence that competition of this requirement would be advantageous to the Government by submitting a capability statement that they have ability to supply the required components meeting the government�s need. If no affirmative written responses are received by 2:00 PM Pacific Time on 05 November 2026, an award will be made without further notice. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. Electronic responses and questions shall be submitted via email to the contracting point of contact listed below. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is not responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. Contracting Office Point of Contact: Nathean Stoner, Nathean.w.stoner@usace.army.mil

Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Solicitation number 127EAX27Q0004 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for updates to the Grizzly Bear Campground. Updates include: Road alignment will be adjusted to accommodate expected traffic, subbase will be enhanced. The water system well will remain; the pumphouse, service and distribution lines, and point-of-use hydrants will be replaced and rerouted to better serve campers. title: Y1DA--VISN 2 EHRM Industry Day
description: Construction Industry Day Introduction In accordance with FAR Companion (FC) 10.001(c), this notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), nor will the VA pay for information requested. Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) will host an industry day event at the James J. Peters Department of Veterans Affairs VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468 for all businesses (including, but not limited to, general contractors, subcontractor trades, and material suppliers) interested in the upcoming Electronic Health Records Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects throughout VISN 2 (NY/NJ). The purpose of the Industry Day is to facilitate collaboration between the VA and general construction contractors and subcontractors of all business sizes who are interested in performing work in New York and New Jersey. This session is designed to give all interested contractors a clear understanding of the project s intent, performance expectations, and execution approach. This industry day will help the VA determine the method of procurement and type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, highlight any industry concerns, gauge general contractor interest in the project, and perform a site walk to show key areas of the Bronx EHRM project. Six EHRM Infrastructure projects were solicited and awarded in FY26. Four of the six were designated as SDVOSB set-asides, and most of these projects received limited bids or proposals. In FY27, VISN 2 anticipates three projects, Bronx, Manhattan, and Northport, that are particularly large and complex, which may pose significant challenges for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) to execute independently due to their scale and technical requirements. As a result, the VA is considering broadening the competition beyond SDVOSBs, seeking participation from both small and/or large businesses that have the project experience, capabilities, and workforce necessary to fulfill the contract demands. This approach is critical to ensuring a robust competitive environment that accurately reflects market value and supports successful project delivery. EVENT INFORMATION The industry day will be held on Thursday, November 19th, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET. The meeting location will be Room 3D-22 in Building 100, located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468. Contractors are required to pre-register for this event. See Administrative section below. Proposed Agenda: 1. Check-in (please arrive between 9 - 9:30 AM) 2. Introductions 3. Meet and Greet 4. Overview of the EHRM Program and Each Project 4. Site walk of the Bronx VAMC EHRM project 5. Lunch Break 6. Questions and answers session 7. Networking *A final agenda will most likely be posted to SAM.gov closer to the event date. PROJECT DESCRIPTIONS VISN 2 (New York/New Jersey) has five EHRM projects that are anticipated to be solicited and awarded in Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 and four in FY 2028. The five planned locations for FY27 are at the following VAMC s: Bronx, Canandaigua, Manhattan, Northport, and St. Albans. A description of each project is listed below. Bronx VAMC: The design modernizes the campus technology backbone and supporting building systems so the medical center can implement the VA EHRM platform while maintaining reliable clinical and facility operations. Work extends across the Main Hospital (Building 100) and multiple adjacent campus buildings and support facilities. A distinguishing feature is the construction of two new telecommunications towers. The towers expand communications capacity and require coordinated architectural, structural, civil, electrical, mechanical, and telecommunications design. The broader project also renovates and expands existing telecommunications and data center spaces and upgrades the supporting power, cooling, fiber, security, and life-safety infrastructure. Canandaigua VAMC: This project comprehensively upgrades the campus s fiber optic network and power distribution systems to meet EHRM design guide requirements, ensuring robust support for clinical and facility operations. The work encompasses fiber network enhancements with redundant routes to each IT closet and the main demarcation room, minimizing risk through parallel systems operation during transitions from legacy to new infrastructure. The project also includes expansion or relocation of telecommunications rooms, installation of 100 new IT outlets and 75 electrical outlets, and substantial improvements in power distribution and HVAC systems. Enhanced physical security is provided through secure data cabinets, protected fiber infrastructure, secured telecommunications rooms, and installation of lockable manhole covers for underground fiber pathways. In addition, hazardous material abatement activities will ensure that all upgraded spaces meet current safety and environmental standards. Manhattan VAMC: The design modernizes telecommunications and IT infrastructure throughout Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and creates resilient power and cooling systems to support continuous healthcare operations and future technology demands. The project relocates the existing data center to renovated space and upgrades 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures. The new data center functions as the campus telecommunications hub and is supported by redundant fiber pathways, dedicated year-round cooling, and 2N UPS and electrical distribution redundancy. These features distinguish the Manhattan project and increase the reliability of critical IT systems. Northport VAMC: This information will be provided in an update to this posting on SAM.gov. St. Albans VAMC: The EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Project at St. Albans VA Medical Center in Queens, NY, is a large-scale modernization effort designed to support the implementation of the VA s new EHRM system. The initiative involves major upgrades across multiple buildings, including the construction of a new data center and telecom tower, extensive electrical and mechanical improvements, and the installation of advanced technology infrastructure such as Cat 6A cabling and a fiber optic backbone, all guided by strict VA standards for compliance, safety, and scalability. Key challenges include managing hazardous materials like asbestos and lead-based paint, addressing spatial and technical constraints in existing telecom rooms, coordinating complex system upgrades within an active healthcare environment, and ensuring meticulous phasing to minimize disruptions. Additionally, the project must integrate diverse building systems, adhere to evolving standards, and provide future-proofing for anticipated growth, all of which add significant complexity to both the design and execution phases. *The following projects anticipated for award in FY28: Albany, Buffalo, Batavia and East Orange. Procurement Information The proposed projects will be a competitive firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as either request for proposals (RFP) in accordance with FAR part 15, considering technical and price factors or Invitation for Bids (IFBs) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering price only. The full acquisition strategy for this proposed project has not yet been developed and will be determined after the industry day and any additional market research is concluded. The targeted cost ranges of each project are listed below. Between $20 and $30 Million: Canandaigua and St. Albans Between $40 and $50 Million: Bronx and Manhattan Between $50 and $60 Million: Northport The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. The project scope includes, but is not limited, to the following infrastructure upgrades: install facility fiber throughout the buildings to each telecommunications Room (TR); provide a redundant fiber run throughout the facility to each TR; provide redundant fiber mains to the demarcation room from the provider point; install approximately 100 additional needed data drops; install approximately 75 new electrical outlets throughout the facility; provide additional power in each TR; upgrade facility power distribution, as required; upgrade facility HVAC distribution, as required; conduct a physical security assessment and provide upgrades; reconfiguration, expansion, and renovation of existing space (demo, new construction, finishes, cable); data center work upgrade fiber infrastructure backbone campus-wide within buildings and between buildings; provide diversified path for WAN; and hazardous material abatement. The requirement is to procure scalable telemetry, tracking and command aperture services to deliver Satellite-to-Ground Communication Services. This requirement supports OSPO in accomplishing its mission of delivering environmental data from remote platforms. The scope encompasses site certification, telemetry downlink data services, and satellite commanding data services to satisfy future NESDIS requirements for commercial remote telemetry downlink for partner missions. Key supported missions include, but are not limited to: COSMIC-2, (the Constellation Observing System for Meteorology Ionosphere and Climate-2)/FORMOSAT-7 KOMPSAT-5, Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite-5 (KOMPSAT-5), and PAZ, Spanish Earth Observation Satellite The proposed contract action will be conducted using other than full and open competition procedures pursuant to the authority at 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 6.103-1,Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will satisfy agency requirements. ATLAS currently holds all active, validated, and fully compliant international spectrum licenses and host-nation operating authorizations across the required equatorial downlink footprint. ATLAS represents the only evaluated source possessing the fully qualified, operational front-end processor architectures, automated scheduling APIs, and verified performance thresholds required to meet NESDIS data delivery requirements without introducing unacceptable integration costs, programmatic delays, and mission-critical data loss risks. title: AF-PLM Capability Integration, Sustainment & Licenses
description: The United States Air Force (USAF) has implemented an Enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solution to modernize the management of weapon systems throughout their lifecycle. This initiative aligns with the Air Force's broader strategic goals to integrate capabilities, revolutionize processes, and enable lifecycle digital material management. The current PLM implementation leverages Siemens Teamcenter, a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution hosted within the Cloud One environment, to empower program offices with centralized, secure, and integrated tools for engineering, manufacturing, sustainment, and asset retirement activities. The USAF continues to face significant challenges in fully realizing seamless PLM integration across its enterprise. These challenges include fragmented legacy systems, disconnected data silos, and a lack of uniformity in processes, all of which contribute to inefficiencies, reduced data integrity, and delays in decision-making. Addressing these issues requires innovative solutions that ensure robust configuration management, streamline workflows, and foster enterprise-wide collaboration while adhering to stringent security and compliance standards. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather industry feedback on technical approaches, market capabilities, and innovative solutions to address these challenges as well as management of licenses required for these capabilities. By engaging with vendors, the USAF seeks to achieve a better understanding of the current state of the market, identify potential pathways for enhancing the AF-PLM capability and license management, and refine its requirements for prospective procurements. Vendor responses will play a critical role in shaping acquisition strategies, identifying feasible solutions, and ensuring that the evolving PLM environment aligns with the USAF's operational and strategic needs. This process supports the overarching goal of achieving an authoritative source of truth for product data and enhancing total lifecycle management for USAF weapon systems. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for Market Research (MR) purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.
